purpose: The accepted acceptance criteria this repository currently binds tests to. It carries no test links: the links are generated from the run, because a maintained criterion-to-test matrix is what STD-0007 forbids. An identifier a test records and this inventory does not declare is reported as drift.

criteria.text: Every source unit in a landed module carries a declared verification tier.
No change lands below its tier's diff branch-coverage floor.
Tier H changed lines reach 100 percent branch coverage and every decision in the validating path is covered to MC/DC.
Coverage is measured with the pinned toolchain and the llvm-cov export JSON is the artifact of record; a rendered report or a quoted percentage is a derived view.
Whole-tree coverage is a verification objective: measured, published with every run, and never gated.
The uncovered set is the review artifact rather than the percentage, and no coverage number is presented as a completion criterion.
No traceability matrix is maintained by hand; the requirements report is generated from executed tests through the recorded requirement property.
Every acceptance criterion is either bound to a named test, listed as unbound, or declared as discharged by a named manual procedure.
Coverage, mutation, and requirement artifacts never appear in the ADR-0019 benchmark chain as a RawRunReceipt, EvidenceSet, EvaluationReceipt, or BaselineRecord.
Every rejection rule in an accepted contract has a named rejection test asserting the specific typed failure.
A coverage floor is never satisfied by deleting or disabling code, by moving code into an exempt classification, or by widening a tier downward.
criteria.procedure: Review of the change: the reviewer compares the declared tier of every touched unit against its previous declaration and against the tier definitions, and rejects a downgrade that the unit's responsibility does not justify.

criteria.text: A test that executes code and asserts nothing about the result is not a test, and a suite of such tests is a defect regardless of the coverage it produces.
criteria.procedure: Review of the change, and the deliberate-break obligation: before a test is complete its author establishes that it fails against a wrong implementation. Mutation testing is the mechanical form and remains blocked on acquisition.

criteria.text: Golden and approval outputs carry a recorded human review from their creation, and regenerating one to pass a failing test is a defect unless the contract change is cited.
criteria.procedure: Review at creation: the reviewer reads the generated bytes once against the contract they claim to express and records the review in the change that introduces them.

criteria.text: Mutation testing is described as practice only after its feasibility experiment against the pinned artifact and its platform decision are recorded.
criteria.procedure: Review of any claim that mutation testing is practice: the reviewer requires the recorded feasibility result and the recorded Windows-lane decision before the claim stands.
